day.text: I withdraw the Finley count, since an Eagle doesn't count its own visit. Blair's Owl list plus Finley's four others makes Alex's visitors Eagle, Kookaburra, Tit, Owl, Mouser. Casey, you're the one who visited Alex, so you're the Mouser by elimination. Casey, confirm your role.
day.note: Blair's Owl list is consistent with the text, and Finley's +4 counts the other four visitors correctly. Only Casey claimed a visit to Alex that matches the Mouser animal, so I now lean toward Casey.

day.text: Yes, I visited Alex. I'm the Hawk, not the Mouser, and my nest didn't change. Blair, your Owl list names a Mouser, and that's the claim you're using to pin me. Blair, what did you actually learn, and were you confused?
day.note: I'm exposed as a visitor to Alex, but admitting Mouser would doom me. I'll concede the visit, claim Hawk, and challenge Blair's Owl list as the weak link.

day.text: Blair, you're pinning a Mouser on Casey using a list that's already been challenged. Casey, if you're the Hawk, a Hawk only gains on a Meowfia target, and Alex is dead now, so that check is gone. Let's not rush a vote on one list.
day.note: Blair and Casey both have claims I can't verify, and my own read is confused. I'll ask for real checks instead of joining a rushed vote.

day.text: Blair's list is the only thing pinning me, and it's already been challenged. Let's look harder at Blair before voting.
day.note: I'm exposed, so I want Blair, who is pinning me, out of the vote. I'll throw my Wild, which costs nothing either way.

day.text: Casey says Hawk and gained nothing, so Alex wasn't Meowfia. That means Blair's list pinning a Mouser on Casey doesn't hold. Blair, what did your Owl visit on Alex show, and who did you actually see? I'm not voting Casey on that list yet.
day.note: Casey's Hawk claim and zero gain on Alex means Alex wasn't Meowfia, so Blair's list naming a Mouser among Alex's visitors can't be fully right. Blair's list has the pinning, so I'll challenge Blair and hold the vote on Casey.
Blair's Owl list is the claim pinning Casey, and Blair's story has the most holes. I'll throw my lowest card at Blair.

day.text: Finley's +4 already counts Casey as one of Alex's visitors, so Casey's Hawk visit fits. Blair's list names a Mouser and leaves out the Hawk, so Blair's Owl read is the wrong one. Blair, did you get confused? I'm leaning toward voting Blair.
day.note: Finley's +4 counts Casey as a visitor, so Casey's Hawk visit fits. Blair's list names a Mouser and omits the Hawk, so Blair's read is the one that's wrong. I'll point at Blair.

day.text: My dawn report had no confusion, and my Owl list was Eagle, Kookaburra, Mouser, Tit. Casey visited Alex, but no Hawk is on that list, so Casey's Hawk claim doesn't match. Casey is the Mouser. I'm voting Casey.
day.note: My dawn report wasn't marked confused, and the Owl list had no Hawk on it, so Casey's Hawk claim fails. The only visitor left unaccounted for is the Mouser, so Casey is the Mouser, and I'm voting Casey.

Alex.note: I'm Farm, and Ellis has been the most suspicious player with the odd Falcon egg. I'll visit Ellis to learn who they visited.

Blair.note: Alex leads with 38 points, so I need to find out who is Meowfia. Visiting Alex shows which animals came to them, which is the most useful check.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia as the Mouser. I'll visit Alex, the score leader, to learn their role and decide how to play this round.

Drew.note: No information yet. I'm visiting Alex, the leader, and guessing Pigeon, the most common Farm role, to test for a payoff.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm as the Kookaburra. Alex is far ahead at 38 and was caught in a false Hawk claim, so I'll visit Alex to learn their role.

Finley.note: I'm the Eagle, so visiting a player shows me who visited them and gains an egg per visitor. Alex is the strongest suspect and leads the table, so I'll visit Alex.

events.text: Animals that visited Alex: Eagle, Kookaburra, Mouser, Tit.
Alex was visited by: Casey, Drew, Ellis, Blair.

audit: Finley lays 4 eggs in Finley's nest

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the visit counts keep shifting, and I'm dead before I can help untangle the Mouser accusation.

Blair.feeling: Messy and frustrating: the claims keep shifting, and I've already had to correct my own read twice.

Casey.feeling: Tense and messy: I'm Meowfia in a round where the table is pinning visits on me, and Blair's Owl list is my best cover.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contested: the Owl, Eagle, and Hawk counts keep conflicting, Alex has collapsed, and I'm unsure whether Blair's Mouser accusation is a real read or a Meowfia smear.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and frustrating: my confused dawn report muddied my own visit read, and the visitor counts keep contradicting each other.

Finley.feeling: Confusing and contradictory: the Eagle and Owl counts keep getting disputed, and Blair and Casey are accusing each other.

Alex.note: I'm dead but my throw still scores. Blair's Owl list has a Mouser visiting Alex, and Casey is the only visitor who isn't on it by role, so Casey is the likely Meowfia. I'll throw one low card at Casey.

Blair.note: Casey is my best read as the Mouser, so I'm throwing two cards at Casey, keeping the high cards.

Casey.note: Blair is pinning me and is the likely Farm target. I'll throw three low cards at Blair to force the vote, keeping my high cards.

Drew.note: Blair's Owl list omits the Hawk and pins a Mouser on Casey, while Finley's count fits Casey's visit, so I'll throw a low card at Blair.

Ellis.note: Casey has changed roles across rounds and claims Hawk now, which contradicts Blair's Owl list that omits any Hawk. I'll switch my low card to Casey.

Finley.note: Blair's Owl list matches what Ellis, Drew and I claimed for three of four visitors, so Blair looks honest and Casey's Hawk claim doesn't fit. I'll throw three Wilds at Casey, which adds three votes at almost no point cost.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle and Owl egg rules were hard to pin down, since it was unclear whether an Eagle counts its own visit and whether an Owl's egg goes to the Owl or the visited player. Several players misread these in the same way, which caused a lot of false accusations.
Alex.fun: Round 2 as the Sphinx: I learned Blair was the Eagle and then watched the table argue over Blair's +2 while I quietly helped keep Blair in the hot seat. Meowfia winning by throwing three high cards at a Farm player was satisfying.
Alex.change: Publish each animal's egg mechanics in one clear reference sheet so players are not arguing over rule text mid-day. Also make Meowfia identities easier to track so the day is less about guessing and more about reasoning.
Alex.regret: In Round 1 I threw my card at Finley, a Farm player, when Ellis was the Floofer Meowfia. I would have thrown at Ellis, since Ellis's Falcon-related accusations were the most suspicious, and I would have trusted my own read over the bandwagon.

Blair.confusing: The Falcon and Eagle egg rules were easy to misread, and whether a visitor's own visit counts toward an Eagle's gain led to several wrong accusations before the table settled it.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when the Owl's visitor list (Eagle, Kookaburra, Mouser, Tit) let me pin the Mouser on Casey, and the table followed the logic to eggsecute them.
Blair.change: Put the animal-to-visitor gain rules in a short reference sheet in every dawn report so players don't have to reconstruct them from memory.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I helped push a throw at Ellis on a Falcon-gain argument that was a misreading. I would instead ask Ellis directly for the source of the +1 before committing cards to a throw.

Casey.confusing: The Falcon's egg rule ("if they visited no one") was easy to misread, and I wrongly accused Alex in round 1 before correcting myself. Also, the Eagle count and whether a visitor's own visit counts took a lot of back-and-forth to pin down.
Casey.fun: Round 2's cross-checking of egg counts against visit claims was satisfying, since Ellis's +1 and Blair's +2 each got traced to a specific visit. Winding up the Mouser's Wink on the score leader in round 3 also felt like a real swing.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports list the specific visitors or effects, so players can check claims without reconstructing each role's rule from memory.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I was Meowfia and used my Wink on Alex, the score leader, but I should have kept the Wink and stayed quiet. Once I'd visited Alex and was exposed, I should have kept my cards instead of throwing three of them at Blair, which didn't save me.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Owl rules were the hardest to read, especially whether an Eagle counts its own visit as a visitor. Several players, including me, got that wrong in the day discussion.
Drew.fun: Round 3's Mouser hunt, where Blair's Owl list and Finley's Eagle count were checked against each other to pin Casey, was the most fun deduction at the table.
Drew.change: I would make dawn reports say exactly which visits produced each egg, so players could check claims without guessing at the rule text.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw at Ellis, a Farm player, when Alex was the real Meowfia; I should have thrown at Alex. In round 3 I threw at Blair, who was Farm, when Casey was the Mouser; I should have thrown at Casey.

Ellis.confusing: Whether an Eagle or Owl counts its own visit, and how the Falcon's egg depends on its target, were easy to misread. Confused dawn reports also made my own role read untrustworthy.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 flipped several times as Alex and Blair pushed accusations, and Alex's Sphinx claim was hard to pin down. Seeing the Hawk and Falcon claims collide was the most fun part.
Ellis.change: I would make the visitor and egg rules explicit in each role's text, including whether an Eagle or Owl counts its own visit. That would cut a lot of table-wide confusion.
Ellis.regret: In Round 2 I misstated my Falcon egg and built a false link to Casey, which muddied the table. I would have stated the rule plainly and asked for the visit counts before accusing anyone.

Finley.confusing: The Falcon and Owl egg rules were hard to track: the Falcon gains only if its target visited no one, and an Owl's egg goes to the Owl's own nest, which made several public claims look contradictory when they were actually fine.
Finley.fun: Round 3's Eagle count was a satisfying puzzle, since Blair's Owl list of Alex's visitors and my +4 slowly forced the table to reconstruct who visited whom.
Finley.change: Make the dawn reports include the source of each egg change (which visitor or animal caused it), so players don't have to reverse-engineer counts from claims.
Finley.regret: In Round 2 I threw at Alex on a Hawk-duplicate argument and Blair was actually Farm; I should have checked the Eagle and Owl counts before pinning anyone. In Round 3 I wasted three Wilds on Casey, but that vote was correct, so the real mistake was Round 1, where I threw at Drew without evidence.

review.title: Misread Eggs, Lucky Wink
review.headline: Everyone argued over egg arithmetic while Alex banked 33 points off one lucky Farm vote.
review.summary: Round 1 was a table-wide fight over how the Falcon works, and it ended with Farm eggsecuting a Farm player. In round 2 Meowfia Alex (Sphinx) claimed Hawk, dumped three high cards on Farm Blair, and won 33 points, which decided the game. In round 3 Casey's Wink killed the leader's chance to talk, but Blair's Owl list pinned Casey and Farm won. Alex was never caught and won easily, 42 to 14.

rounds.recap: Four players piled onto Alex because they misread the Falcon text. Most of them retracted by beat 4, but the votes were already scattered. Farm Drew was eggsecuted, mostly by Finley's two cards, and lone Meowfia Ellis won with a Wild thrown.

Alex, the Meowfia Sphinx, claimed Hawk, and Finley's real Hawk claim clashed with it. Players then misread the Eagle text, and Blair's correct +2 became the suspicious claim. Alex threw 33 points at Blair, and Casey joined him, so Blair was eggsecuted and Meowfia won big.

Casey the Mouser winked the Falcon Alex, who was the score leader. Blair's Owl list and Finley's Eagle +4 pointed at Casey as the unlisted visitor. Casey claimed Hawk, but three Wilds from Finley and other throws sank Casey, and Farm won.

highlights.text: Alex threw 12, 8 and 13 at Blair, a known Farm Eagle, and banked 33 points for the win.
Casey winked Alex, the 38-point leader, mid-day. The table never even asked who did it.
Blair's Owl list of four animals plus Finley's +4 Eagle gain fit together and exposed the Mouser by elimination.
The table turned on Alex over the Falcon egg, then everyone checked the text and reversed within one day.

confusions.what: Said a Falcon gains only if it visited no one, then later conceded the egg depends on the target.
Misread the Falcon, said a Turkey's unchanged nest proved nobody visited, then retracted.
Misread the Falcon and threw at Alex before retracting.
Misread the Falcon, and also said the Owl report listed no visitors, which was odd.
Misread the Falcon and backed the Alex accusation.
Tied a Falcon's egg to its own visit, then corrected it.
Said an Owl's egg lands in the target's nest, which is right, but then counted Blair as a third visitor to Casey.
Said Casey's Owl egg goes in the Owl's own nest, which is wrong for Owl.
Misdescribed how the Eagle counts visitors, then partly backed Casey's wrong version.
Said an Eagle's gain is per visitor to the Eagle itself, which is wrong.
Claimed Blair had three visitors to Casey including Blair, which is wrong because an Eagle's own visit isn't counted.
Said Finley's count should be five and that an Owl learns only its own visitors, then withdrew the first point.
Repeated the five-visitors miscount for Finley's Eagle gain.
Concluded Casey's claimed Hawk zero-gain means Alex wasn't Meowfia, which is wrong because Alex was Farm anyway and tells nothing about Casey.

worked: Mouser's Wink: Casey removed the 38-point leader in round 3 and the table barely reacted. It is a strong, clean action.
Owl visitor lists plus Eagle gains gave round 3 a real puzzle. The animal list and the +4 cross-checked and led to Casey.
Throw counts as public signals and the consolation return: Finley's low-cost Wild throws and the returned best cards kept even losing throws meaningful.
Hidden Meowfia count and Meowfia not knowing each other: Casey and Alex never coordinated, which kept the lies honest.
problems: Round 2 scoring snowballs: Alex banked 33 points from one win and nobody could catch up. The win condition is decided in one round. Consider capping banked cards, or a catch-up rule for the leader.

Role texts are too hard to read. Falcon, Eagle and Owl wording caused misreads by almost every player in every round. Rewrite them as: 'Falcon gains if its target visited no one' and 'Eagle gains per visitor to its target, not counting itself'.
Alex was never punished as the leader or the winner. The 38-point leader can throw big at a Farm player and still win. Add a risk to winning throws, or a cost for throwing high on the losing side.
Mouser's Wink gives no cost. Nobody traces who winked, so there is no deduction from it, and it just silently kills the best speaker. Consider a tell, such as the winker's nest size changing.
Round 1 was mostly noise. Several players wrongly accused Alex, then flipped. Rule misreads drive play more than reasoning, so voting is arbitrary. Add a short role card with worked examples.
